rows.statement: Across Michigan and New York census tracts in 2020-2024, age-standardized disability prevalence (2000 U.S. standard population) is higher where the poverty rate is higher, with state intercepts; coefficient corrected for ACS sampling error in both variables (fit_eiv).

Conditional on the poverty rate, the share of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher, the housing cost-burden share and state, age-standardized disability prevalence is higher where a larger share of occupied housing units has no vehicle available (fit_eiv).

Conditional on the poverty rate, the bachelor's share, the no-vehicle share and state, age-standardized disability prevalence is higher where a larger share of households spends 30% or more of income on housing costs (renters and owners, among households with the ratio computed) (fit_eiv).
